The RS and Clocked RS flip-flops have limitations which make them unsuitable for many digital circuits.
INTRODUCTIONM
The RS and Clocked RS flip-flops have separate inputs for S and R.
The D-Type flip-flop has one input that is used for both the S and R inputs.
Let's begin the lesson on D-Type FLIP-FLOP................................
LESSON MENU
The D-Type flip-flop is designed to store the last input condition until the next input condition is gated through.
DISCUSSION
D-Type flip-flops have two inputs and two outputs.
A high applied to the DATA or D input sets the output state to a high Q when the clock input is high.
A low applied to the D input sets the output state to a low Q when the clock input is high..
When the clock input is low, the D input is disabled and the flip-flop stays in its current state.
The D-Type flip-flop is a good replacement for a set of mechanical switches that are used to indicate binary numbers.
The binary number 101 closes switches S1 and S3 applying a high to lights 1 and 3.
The D flip-flop can replace the mechanical switches, producing the same results.

This D-Type flip-flop is constructed from four NAND gates and an inverter. D-Type flip-flops may also be constructed from NOR gates and an inverter.
Note that gates A, B, C and D form a NAND gate Clocked RS flip-flop.
Adding a single input that is applied directly to gate A and inverted and applied to gate B, makes a D flip-flop.
A high D input places a high on gate A and a low on gate B. This condition causes a low output from gate A when the clock is high.
The low output from gate A is inverted by gate C setting Q high. Remember, any low input to a NAND gate will produce a high output.
A low D input places a low on gate A and a high on gate B. This condition causes a low output from gate B when the clock is high.
The low output from gate B is inverted by gate D setting Q high.

This experiment demonstrates the operation of a D-Type Flip-Flop. You will enter input signals for DATA and CLOCK and probe the outputs of the flip-flop to verify the correct output signals at Q and Q.signals.
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-114 card. The purpose of this card is to demonstrate the operation of a D-Type flip-flop.
The PC130-111 Clock/Pulser Card is used to supply the clock and data inputs to the flip-flop.
With PC130-111 S2 in the PULSER position a pulse is applied to the flip-flop CLOCK input on PC130-114 only when C130-111 S1 is pressed.
With PC130-111 S3 in the 1 position a high is applied to the flip-flop on PC130-114 DATA input.
With PC130-111 S3 in the 0 position a low is applied to the flip-flop on PC130-114 DATA input.
Switches PC130-114 S1 and S2 must be in the operate (OP) position for normal operation of the flip-flop.
With PC130-114 S1 in SET, a low is applied to the set side of the flip-flop causing the flip-flop to set.
With PC130-114 S2 in CLR (clear), a low is applied to the reset side of the flip-flop which causes it to reset. Let's begin the experiment.
